name: Meshullam
overview: Meshullam was a male Levite of the Kohathite clan who served as a foreman overseeing the reconstruction of the Temple during the reign of King Josiah. His leadership role in this significant restoration project highlights his importance within the Levitical community and the religious reforms of that period.
namesAndTitles: The name Meshullam means 'restitution' and is a proper name used in Scripture. This meaning aligns with his role in the restoration efforts of the Temple, symbolizing a return to proper worship and covenant faithfulness.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Meshullam as a descendant of Kohath, placing him within the Kohathite branch of the Levites. Beyond this lineage, no additional family relationships are recorded.
scriptureSignificance: Meshullam's significance lies in his leadership during a pivotal moment of religious renewal under King Josiah, as he was entrusted with the vital task of overseeing the Temple's reconstruction. As a Kohathite Levite, his role underscores the involvement of the priestly families in restoring the house of God, reflecting the biblical emphasis on faithful stewardship of worship and covenantal heritage.
